svg.title: Stepwise NEST control: overhead, speed and threading under NEST 3.10.0
svg.desc: Three panels measured on 13 October 2026 with NEST 3.10.0 on an Apple MacBook Pro with an M4 Max chip and 128 GB of memory, at NCP commit 6feba8d. Panel a: prepared 1 ms chunks cost 1.10 times one Run call, 10 ms chunks 1.008 times and 100 ms chunks 1.002 times; a NEST 3.9.0 build gave 1.145 in the same session and 1.448 on 7 October. Panel b: biological seconds per wall-clock second for 1, 4 and 8 threads from 2,000 to 20,000 neurons, with the same-session NEST 3.9.0 build as open circles. Panel c: a Python counter retains 1.4 percent of its rate around nest.Run, and serial-to-threaded period ratios are 0.91 to 0.99.

g.font-family: 'Source Sans Pro', 'Source Sans 3', 'Latin Modern Math', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
g.text: STEPWISE NEST CONTROL · OVERHEAD, SPEED AND THREADING
NEST 3.10.0 on one workstation; NCP benchmark scripts at 6feba8d; (a,b) minimum times; (c) one probe and loop pair.
(c) Can Python overlap transport with a running kernel?
1.4% retained in one probe around Run()
Source: rerun of NCP's bench_chunk_overhead.py, bench_realtime.py and bench_overlap.py on 13 October 2026; values are indicative, not calibrated.
